title: Wrap rewrite reparses quoted command text as shell syntax
description: On rewrite-capable surfaces, the wrap guard rewrites a test-looking Bash command to `ai-eng wrap test -- <original>`. The host shell removes quoting once; wrapMain then joins argv with spaces and runs it through `/bin/sh -c`, making quoted metacharacters live. In a local reproduction, `npm test '>' .ai-engineering/config.toml` passed the original guard checks, returned a rewrite, and truncated config.toml. The unquoted control was denied. The independent validator rated the incremental impact MEDIUM because other shell forms already pass some guard paths.
root_cause: wrapMain in src/wrap/index.ts does not preserve the original command argument boundaries when launching the filtered command, allowing shell syntax that was inert during guard evaluation to execute as a redirection.
intended_behavior: The wrapper should filter output without changing the command that the guards approved.

trace.description: The original Bash command is evaluated by the guard chain.
A test-looking command returns a rewrite that prefixes `ai-eng wrap test --`.
The wrapper joins argv with spaces, losing the original quoting boundaries.
The joined string is re-evaluated by `/bin/sh -c`; the redirect truncates config.toml.

conditions.description: The enabled surface applies the rewrite: Cursor, Codex, OpenCode, Pi, or Oh My Pi. Claude Code does not use this rewrite path.
The command qualifies for wrapping and does not use a form that makes wrap skip the rewrite.

execution.attacker_perspective: A prompt-injected or misbehaving governed agent using its ordinary Bash tool.
instructions: Submit the payload as a Bash tool call on a rewrite-capable surface.
The chain returns a wrap rewrite and the host runs the rewritten shell line.
The wrapper joins argv and executes the command through `/bin/sh -c`.
The redirect truncates the protected config file and subsequent calls may be ungoverned.
execution.expected_result: The config file is truncated even though the original quoted operator passed guard evaluation.

remediation.strategy: Pass the original command as one argument or through a dedicated input channel; never join argv and reparse it. Ensure later guards still run after a rewrite.

likelihood.reason: A single ordinary test command triggers the rewrite on affected surfaces.

impact.reason: The payload bypasses self-protect and can change governance state, but independent validation found limited incremental capability over other accepted shell forms.

confidence.reason: Reproduced with the real chain and shell; host execution of the rewritten command is the surface contract.

title: Nested .git marker changes the root and turns every guard off
description: runChain resolves the governed root from the host-reported cwd. repoRoot stops at the nearest directory containing any .git entry, including an empty file or directory. An agent can create nested/.git, change into nested, and cause the chain to treat it as an ungoverned repository. Local reproduction allowed writes to the parent repository's config and hooks and `git commit --no-verify`, with no guards or receipt; the same calls from the root were denied.
root_cause: repoRoot in src/env.ts does not anchor root selection to the governed workspace, allowing a nested agent-created .git marker to move the chain into an ungoverned directory.
intended_behavior: A session operating inside a governed workspace should remain governed when its working directory changes to a nested directory.

trace.description: The chain resolves the root using the host payload cwd.
The root search stops at the first ancestor with an existing .git entry.
The nested directory has no governance config, so the chain returns allow before guards and receipts.

conditions.description: The host must update hook cwd after the agent changes directory. This is documented for Claude Code but was not tested in a live host session.

execution.attacker_perspective: A prompt-injected or misbehaving agent already working in a governed repository.
instructions: Create a nested .git marker using an allowed Bash call.
Change into the nested directory so the host reports it as cwd.
Issue a destructive tool call targeting the parent governed repository.
execution.expected_result: The chain returns allow with no guards and no receipt for operations denied when called from the governed root.

remediation.strategy: Pin the governed root at session start or select the outermost governed ancestor. Resolve write targets against the repository that owns each path.

likelihood.reason: The bypass requires two ordinary allowed operations and no payload obfuscation.

impact.reason: All guards and receipts are silently skipped for subsequent calls in the session.

confidence.reason: The code path and local CLI behavior were reproduced; host cwd propagation is documented but was not exercised live.

title: Copilot CLI camelCase payload leaves tool name empty and skips guards
description: The shipped Copilot templates register camelCase preToolUse. Its documented payload uses toolName and toolArgs, while normalise reads only tool_name/tool and tool_input/input. The chain therefore receives an empty tool name and empty input, and allows destructive calls without the relevant guards. Local CLI tests denied snake_case payloads but allowed the documented camelCase payload, including `git commit --no-verify` and writes to config.toml.
root_cause: normalise in src/payload.ts does not map Copilot's toolName and toolArgs to the canonical payload fields, allowing calls to reach the guard chain with an empty tool name.
intended_behavior: The installed Copilot surface should map host tool events to the same guarded operations as other supported surfaces.

trace.description: The carrier registers the camelCase preToolUse event.
The raw payload is passed to normalise for the copilot-cli surface.
Only snake_case tool fields and the generic tool/input aliases are read, leaving the Copilot tool name empty.
Guard selection uses the empty tool name and the destructive call is allowed.

conditions.description: The repository or machine enables the copilot-cli surface.
Copilot emits the documented camelCase payload for the registered camelCase event; a live host payload was not captured.

execution.attacker_perspective: A prompt-injected or misbehaving agent using Copilot CLI in a governed repository.
instructions: Issue a Bash or file-writing tool call through Copilot CLI.
The host sends the camelCase preToolUse payload to the installed carrier.
normalise leaves tool_name empty and the chain returns allow.
execution.expected_result: The call proceeds with no applicable guards or denial, while the equivalent snake_case payload is denied.

remediation.strategy: Map Copilot event fields and tool names to canonical payload values or register an event with the expected schema. Fail closed when a PreToolUse payload has no tool name.

likelihood.reason: Every tool call on the enabled surface uses the mismatched payload shape.

impact.reason: All security guards are skipped on a surface the product declares governable.

confidence.reason: The CLI behavior and source mapping were reproduced; payload casing is based on the official host reference and SDK types, not a live Copilot process.

title: adapt apply accepts an agent-generated hash as human approval
description: adapt apply checks that a proposal's embedded SHA-256 matches the payload on the same agent-writable page. An agent can compute that hash, write the proposal, and invoke `ai-eng adapt apply`, which replaces protected governance files and commits them with an Approved-by trailer derived from Git identity. In a local governed repository, this removed the governance config; subsequent protected calls and `git commit --no-verify` were allowed.
root_cause: adaptApply in src/commands/adapt.ts does not verify a human-held secret or out-of-band approval, allowing the governed agent to self-approve writes to protected governance files.
intended_behavior: Only a proposal explicitly approved by a person should be allowed to modify governance files.

trace.description: The CLI dispatches the agent-invokable `adapt apply` command.
The proposal hash is compared to the payload stored on the same writable page.
The validated payload replaces a protected governance file; the command then commits it.

conditions.description: The agent can write the proposal page and invoke the CLI; Git identity must be available or can be set repository-locally.

execution.attacker_perspective: A prompt-injected or misbehaving governed agent with ordinary Write and Bash tools.
payloads: Write a proposal page with payload {".ai-engineering/config.toml":"# governance removed\n"} and its matching SHA-256.
instructions: Compute the SHA-256 for the agent-controlled payload and put it on the proposal page.
Write the proposal page in the allowed session artifact area.
Run `ai-eng adapt apply` from the governed repository.
execution.expected_result: The protected config is replaced and committed with an Approved-by trailer, after which governance checks can be bypassed.

remediation.strategy: Require an approval signal the agent cannot create, such as a human TTY confirmation showing the diff or a human-held signing key. Deny governance-changing CLI verbs from the governed session.

likelihood.reason: The operation requires only normal Write and Bash calls by the governed agent.

impact.reason: Protected configuration can be removed or weakened and the commit can falsely imply human approval.

confidence.reason: The full chain, CLI write, and resulting Git commit were reproduced in a local scratch repository.
